title: The Apostle's Embassy and the Daily Working
summary: The Apostle's embassy against the proprium's primal motion and the daily working of light. T74 names envy as the first nature of the proprium — the original shape of self-love, the first motion of the claiming self. T75 sets against it the Eight Dwellings of Living Love — divine love at every register from the natural ground to the visible cosmic signs. T76 reads the Apostle's salutation as the cosmic letter between Call and Hearing — the structural conversation between the Lord and the soul. T77 names the four kingdoms of the world, none exalted exceedingly above the rest. T78 unfolds the four great works of self-love (appetite, joining, possession, dominion) and the separation that lifts the soul above them. T79 describes how light comes in and works through the soul by daily purification. T80 names the two faces shown forth in the rational — love and the strife being refined.
organizing_principle: The contrast of envy as first nature of the proprium (T74) with love as fire at eight registers (T75) opens the section; the Apostle's embassy follows (T76 peace as cosmic letter, T77 the limited kingdoms, T78 the four great works of sin); and the section closes with the daily reception (T79) and the two faces by which the soul shows itself in formation (T80). The arc moves from the proprium's primal claim through the Apostle's response to the daily working out of regeneration.
